author: J.E.Gray & G.R.Gray, 1863
status: 텃새 수천 마리 · 나그네새 수십 마리
habitat: 자갈이 많은 하천과 강가, 강가의 자갈밭과 모래밭
summary: 강가의 자갈밭이나 모래밭에서 국지적으로 번식하는 텃새이다. 꼬마물떼새와 비슷한 환경에 살지만 자갈이 더 많은 하천과 강가를 찾으며, 홀로 또는 작은 무리로 지낸다. 자갈 사이 땅을 오목하게 파서 둥지를 만들고 알 4개를 낳아 28~29일 동안 품는다. 국외에서는 우수리 지방과 중국 동북부에서 번식하고 중국 남부와 인도 북부에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Long-billed Plover (Charadrius placidus), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean gravel riverbeds from March to July: forehead white; a black bar across the forecrown between the eyes; crown and nape grey-brown; narrow whitish supercilium behind the eye; lores and ear-coverts dusky dark brown, not a solid black mask; white throat continuing into a white collar around the hindneck; below it a narrow black breast band, narrowest at the centre of the breast; rest of the underparts white. Upperparts plain grey-brown. Bill long and slender, black with a small pale area at the base of the lower mandible. Thin, faint yellow eye-ring. Legs dull yellowish.
art.pose: standing on river shingle, side view
art.scene: Korean riverbed of gravel and sand beside a shallow flowing stream; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view standing on gravel: long slender black bill, thin faint yellow eye-ring, black forecrown bar, dusky brown ear-coverts, white collar, narrow black breast band narrowing at the centre, long dull yellowish legs, tail projecting beyond the wingtips
adult, head detail in side view: pale base to the lower mandible, thin faint yellow eye-ring, dusky lores, white forehead below the black forecrown bar
art.build: Medium-sized ringed plover, 20.5cm, clearly larger, longer-legged and longer-tailed than Little Ringed Plover. Rounded head, slim body with a long rear end. Bill black and slender, noticeably longer and finer than in Little Ringed Plover. Legs fairly long, dull yellowish. At rest the tail projects well beyond the wingtips. In flight only a faint, narrow white wing bar; tail long, with white sides and a dark subterminal band. Runs and pauses among pebbles at the river's edge.
avoid: Do not paint a solid black mask through the eye and a thick bright yellow eye-ring — that is Little Ringed Plover.
Do not paint a short stubby bill or an orange bill base like Common Ringed Plover.
Do not paint orange legs or a bold white wing bar.
Do not break the breast band into side patches (Kentish Plover); the black band is complete, only narrower at the centre.
